messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: metering - sudden overage flags for ~120 customers; alert source=overage-detector, window=15m. Pager routed to metering-oncall.

alex.k: i'm on it. seeing a burst in token_emitter_rate from emitter-proxy cluster in us-west-2, unusual duplication pattern. spikes correlate with deploy at 07:10 UTC.

maria_g: @alex.k which deploy? i can pull logs and query the aggregator.

alex.k: deploy user/retry-proxy:v2.3.4. quick check: 
```
# top suspicious emitter ids
SELECT emitter_id, count(*) AS c, min(ts) AS first_ts, max(ts) AS last_ts
FROM prod_metering.token_emits
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY emitter_id
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY c DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

alex.k: results show a handful of emitter_ids with thousands of duplicates in 10m. looks like the proxy retried and re-emitted without idempotency keys.

jordan-sre: looking at metrics: token_count_total jumped +22% vs baseline; emitter_ack_latency is normal. suspect duplicate ingestion, not upstream model behavior. wavefront query: `ts("metering.token_emits.count", filter=emitter=proxy) by (emitter_id)` shows repeated bursts.

billing-eng: customers started receiving overage emails ~07:30 UTC; CS flagged multiple enterprise customers. we should pause automated overage notifications until we confirm.

cs-lead: i've got support reps standing by; please tag list of affected customers so we can proactively reach out if needed.

ops-amy: can we stop the overages quickly? options: 1) pause overage notifications in billing service; 2) stop the ingest stream to recon pipeline; 3) apply de-dup filter on downstream aggregator.

maria_g: quick mitigation plan:
- step A: disable overage emails (billing service feature toggle) -> reduce customer unrest.
- step B: enable dedupe on aggregator: drop events with same (emitter_id, request_id) within 1h window.
- step C: replay clean events from raw store after fix.

alex.k: i'm going to open a short-lived proxy rollback to v2.3.3 to stop new duplicates. i'll coordinate with deploy-bot.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: starting rollback of user/retry-proxy to v2.3.3 in us-west-2.

alex.k: rollback started. PATCH: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/retry-proxy --to-revision=42 (monitoring).

jordan-sre: i've pushed a transient server-side dedupe patch to aggregator that ignores identical (emitter_id, payload_hash) events seen within 60m. patch id=met-dup-2026-03-15-01. warming up, will take effect within seconds.

billing-eng: feature toggle "billing.overage_emails" -> OFF. Confirmed: notification queue drained and halted.

cs-lead: thanks. please post final affected-customer list. i'm prepping templated message for enterprise customers.

alex.k: rollback completed at ~07:48 UTC, new duplicate rate dropped to baseline.

maria_g: verifying ingest: run this to estimate duplicate volume and impacted customers:
```
WITH dups AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS dup_count
  FROM prod_metering.token_emits
  WHERE ts BETWEEN now() - interval '2 hours' AND now() - interval '30 minutes'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > expected_baseline(customer_id) * 1.15
)
SELECT customer_id, dup_count FROM dups ORDER BY dup_count DESC LIMIT 200;
```

maria_g: preliminary list: 117 customers with >10% excess tokens in the window; top 10 include: acme-corp, finlytics, edu-labs, chatflow-inc. exporting full CSV to #private-billing.

billing-eng: note: some customers already billed automatically by the overage job at 08:00 UTC. we'll need a reconciliation and potential credit issuance. initiating Billing Incident (BI-2026-119).

ops-amy: replay plan: snapshot raw bucket to dedupe-job, run aggregator with idempotency checks, generate corrected delta ingestion for invoices. this will take ~3-4 hours.

jordan-sre: risk assessment: replay may double-process if dedupe is not perfect; we'll run a dry-run first and compare aggregates. Also root cause: retry-proxy didn't attach idempotency-token on retry path when backend 5xx happened. filing ticket: PROXY-456.

alex.k: quick patch to proxy will add idempotency-header on retries; PR open and merging to main with test. but we already rolled back so immediate risk mitigated.

oncall-bot: escalation: oncall shift ending in 25m. handoff required.

alex.k: handing off to @jordan-sre for next shift. summary: duplicate emits caused by retry-proxy v2.3.4 -> rollback done, billing emails paused, dedupe patch applied to aggregator, replay scheduled, billing team opened BI-2026-119 for reconciliation. impacted ~117 customers; top-10 provided to CS.

jordan-sre: acknowledged. i'll take ownership for replay and reconciliation tracking. setting a runbook entry and will update every 30m until resolved. tagging @billing-eng for follow-ups.

billing-eng: assign BI-2026-119 to me, will coordinate credits and customer communication, ETA for first reconciliation draft: 4 hours.

cs-lead: will send holding message to affected enterprise customers (no billing changes yet) and follow up once BI team confirms credits.

jordan-sre: leaving a short checklist for next oncall:
- verify dedupe patch metrics: `metering.dedup.rate` trending >0 for 10m then ->0 once backlog drained
- monitor `billing.overage_emails.sent` remains 0 until billing gives go-ahead
- validate replay dry-run aggregated totals against pre-incident baselines
- run postmortem template and link PROXY-456 and BI-2026-119

ops-amy: thanks for the handoff. i'll watch the replay job logs and coordinate with storage for raw snapshot access.

jordan-sre: closing console handoff at 08:12 UTC. next update in #incidents and BI ticket. :white_check_mark: 

oncall-bot: NOTE: follow-up reminder scheduled in 3h for postmortem draft.

maria_g: leaving final note: save all raw messages, do not drop the original raw bucket until reconciliation completes.

cs-lead: acknowledged. will not notify customers about credits until BI confirms numbers.

alex.k: thanks everyone. if any urgent customer pings come in mention @billing-eng and @cs-lead.

billing-eng: acknowledging. starting credit calc job now.

jordan-sre: handed off. signing out for this shift.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from several participants)
